messages.text:
Trestle Freight is prepared to move Mara into ownership of the internal security platform on the following terms, which we can put in a recommendation package if they work on your side.

Base salary: $180,000. Signing: $12,000, paid with the first payroll after start, if she starts on or before May 19 so she has a real runway before the July audit. If the earliest realistic start is June 2, signing drops to $8,000; later than June 16 is not workable for the audit.

On-site: two three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks, travel covered by Trestle. We are not asking for weekly presence.

Incident coverage: business hours only, conditioned on Mara training a named escalation partner before the first on-call handoff, with that training finished in the first three weeks.

Scope is ownership of the internal security platform, continuing the identity-modernization work she already led, reporting into security leadership. No equity change is on the table in this package.

If base, start date, or the on-site pattern is the constraint, say which term you need to move and what you would trade. We will not reopen incident coverage without the escalation-partner training.

I could recommend a June 1 start to Mara at a $185,000 base with a $12,000 signing payment on the first payroll. The signing payment replaces a vest she would forfeit by starting June 1. At $8,000, her available start is July 1, beyond your audit cutoff.

In exchange for the June 1 start, Mara can commit to two three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks, with Trestle covering travel. After that, we propose remote work with any visits grouped into at most two trips per month, scheduled by mutual agreement and covered by Trestle. We can leave equity as offered.

Please put security architecture ownership in the written scope. Mara would own the internal platform’s security architecture and roadmap, including identity modernization, and report to security leadership.

Mara can train an escalation partner within her first three weeks, before the first on-call handoff. That commitment depends on Trestle naming the partner and reserving their training time before Mara starts. Please confirm who will cover after-hours incidents during training and if the handoff is delayed. With business-hours coverage for Mara throughout and those staffing commitments in writing, I could recommend the package.

We can recommend this package.

Base $185,000. Start June 1. Signing $12,000 on the first payroll, tied to that start date. That uses the signing money to cover the vest she would forfeit by starting ahead of the July audit. We will not increase signing above $12,000 at this base and date.

First 12 weeks: two three-day site visits per month, travel covered by Trestle. After that, remote, with any further visits by mutual agreement, at most two trips per month, and Trestle covers pre-approved travel. No standing monthly travel obligation after week 12.

Written scope: Mara owns the internal security platform’s security architecture and roadmap, including identity modernization, and reports to security leadership. This is platform ownership, not company-wide security architecture outside that platform. Equity unchanged.

Incident coverage: business hours only for Mara throughout. Trestle will name the escalation partner and reserve their training time in the offer, before she starts. Current on-call coverage handles all after-hours incidents until training is complete and the handoff is written. Training finishes within her first three weeks; the handoff is not made, and she is not placed on after-hours coverage, until that training is done. If the named partner is unavailable for the reserved time, Trestle reschedules inside those three weeks rather than putting Mara on after-hours.

If those points match what you can recommend, we will write them that way. The only open item we still need from you is confirmation that June 1, $185,000, and $12,000 signing close it.

Yes. A June 1 start, a $185,000 base, and a $12,000 signing payment on the first payroll close the compensation and start-date discussion. I recommend the full package to Mara on the terms you’ve set out. Please issue the written offer on those terms, including the escalation partner’s name and reserved training time.

One open travel term before we issue the offer. Trestle will fund four hotel nights per visit. The first 12 weeks stay two three-day visits per month, but one of those visits before the July audit must be at a second site, not only headquarters.

We need a location schedule we can write down: which of the six visits is the second site, which site, and which dates in June or early July. Nights beyond four on any visit are not in the travel budget. If a visit runs longer, Mara covers the excess nights, or we shorten that visit to four nights and keep the three on-site days by arriving the morning of day one.

Confirm the second-site date and that excess nights sit with Mara, and we will put both in the written offer with the rest of the agreed package.

I propose using the first July visit for five consecutive on-site days at the second site, July 1–5, and removing the second June trip. That makes the second-site visit Mara’s second trip overall and brings the 12-week total to five visits. Mara can arrive on day one and depart on day five. Please confirm the site name and address, that the site can host her on all five dates, and that the visit finishes before the audit. If those dates don’t work, please propose a five-day block that does, with the same June trip removed.

Four Trestle-funded hotel nights per visit works. Mara will cover any extra nights she chooses for personal reasons. If the required itinerary would take more than four nights, we’ll adjust the dates or travel times together.

For sign-off, please include two dates in the offer:

- **After-hours handover.** Please specify the planned handover date within Mara’s first three weeks, alongside the partner’s name and reserved training time. Current on-call staff retain after-hours coverage until training is complete and the handover is documented. Mara’s coverage stays within business hours throughout.
- **Travel reimbursement.** I propose that Trestle reimburse covered expenses within 10 business days after Mara submits receipts for each visit. If Trestle uses a fixed payment cycle, please specify the receipt deadline and corresponding payment date.

I can recommend the package with those details in writing and the previously agreed compensation, start date, and platform scope.

We will not drop the second June trip or convert the first July visit into a five-day second-site block. The June 1 start and the signing payment are for presence before the July audit. Two three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks stays as agreed. There is no second site in this assignment, so I will not put a site name, address, or a July 1–5 host commitment in the offer. Visits are to Trestle’s primary office; the offer will state that office address. A five-day block is not required and is not accepted.

Hotel: Trestle funds up to three nights per three-day visit. A fourth night is covered only if the booked itinerary cannot be completed in three, agreed before booking. Extra nights for personal reasons are Mara’s.

After-hours handover date: June 19. That is inside the first three weeks from the June 1 start. The written offer will name the escalation partner and list the reserved training time before she starts; I will not issue it without those. Current on-call keeps all after-hours coverage until training is complete and the handover is documented. Mara remains business-hours only throughout. If the named partner misses the reserved time, Trestle reschedules inside those three weeks and the June 19 handover moves only as far as needed inside that window. She is not placed on after-hours coverage if it slips.

Travel reimbursement: Trestle pays covered expenses within 10 business days after she submits receipts for that visit.

Compensation, start date, and platform scope are unchanged: $185,000 base, June 1, $12,000 signing on the first payroll, platform security architecture and roadmap including identity modernization, reporting to security leadership.

Confirm you can recommend on that visit pattern, the June 19 handover date, and the reimbursement timing. The partner’s name goes in the offer, not in this exchange.

Yes. I can recommend the package to Mara with two three-day visits per month at Trestle’s primary office for the first 12 weeks. Please include the office address and the hotel terms you specified. After week 12, Mara works remotely, with up to two trips per month by mutual agreement and pre-approved travel covered by Trestle.

June 19 works as the planned after-hours handover date. The offer should name the escalation partner and list the reserved training time. Current on-call staff retain after-hours coverage until training is complete and the handover is documented, including if the date slips. Mara’s incident coverage stays within business hours throughout.

Reimbursement within 10 business days after Mara submits receipts for each visit works. Please issue the written offer on those terms, with the June 1 start, $185,000 base, $12,000 signing payment on the first payroll, and ownership of the internal security platform’s architecture and roadmap, including identity modernization, reporting to security leadership.

The commercial terms are closed. We will issue the written offer on that basis. I had not previously specified an office street address or hotel policy, so those go in as follows rather than as if they were already agreed.

Offer terms:

- Start: June 1.
- Base: $185,000.
- Signing: $12,000 on the first payroll, conditioned on the June 1 start.
- Scope: ownership of the internal security platform’s security architecture and roadmap, including identity modernization, reporting to security leadership. Not company-wide architecture outside that platform. Equity unchanged.
- First 12 weeks: two three-day visits per month at Trestle Freight’s primary office. The formal offer will insert the street address HR has on file; I will not put a placeholder address in this package.
- Lodging: one standard business-hotel room per visit night, booked by Trestle or reimbursed at actual reasonable cost, plus pre-approved travel. No luxury or extended-stay upgrade.
- After week 12: remote. Further visits only by mutual agreement, at most two trips per month, pre-approved travel covered on the same basis.
- Reimbursement: within 10 business days after Mara submits receipts for each visit.
- Incidents: Mara’s coverage is business hours only throughout. Planned after-hours handover date is June 19, inside the first three weeks. The formal offer will name the escalation partner and list the reserved training blocks before she starts. Current on-call staff keep all after-hours coverage until training is complete and the handover is documented, including if June 19 slips. She is not placed on after-hours coverage if the date moves. If the named partner misses the reserved time, Trestle reschedules inside the three weeks.

That is the package we will recommend. Partner name, reserved training blocks, and the primary-office street address are the only inserts left for the formal offer document.
